title: status.nominatedNodeName is now set for every pod the scheduler is about to bind, and cleared after binding

detection.reason: which controllers read nominatedNodeName is a runtime behaviour, not a collected object

quote: Enabled the `NominatedNodeNameForExpectation` feature in kube-scheduler by default.
remediation: Controllers that treat a populated `nominatedNodeName` as "a preemption is in flight" (some autoscalers, custom schedulers, dashboards) see it on ordinary pods for the duration of binding. Update that logic or disable `NominatedNodeNameForExpectation` on kube-scheduler.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.nominatedNodeName != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " -> " + .status.nominatedNodeName'  # after the upgrade this list is transient binding state, not only preemption
coversNotes: Enabled the `ClearingNominatedNodeNameAfterBinding` feature in kube-apiserver by default.

title: Components refuse to start when an enabled feature gate depends on a disabled one (AllAlpha=true now needs AllBeta=true)

detection.reason: the feature-gate list lives in a component config file or flag on the control plane host, which is not a Kubernetes object the agent collects; the command reads it from the static pod's command line

quote: A feature can no longer be enabled if it depends on a disabled feature. In particular, this means that `AllAlpha=true` will no longer work without enabling disabled-by-default beta features that are depended on
remediation: Review every `--feature-gates` / `featureGates:` setting on kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler and the kubelets: an alpha gate enabled while its beta dependency is off, or `AllAlpha=true` without `AllBeta=true`, stops the component from starting after the upgrade.
verifyCommand: { kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-apiserver -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.containers[].command[]?, .items[].spec.containers[].args[]?'; kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-controller-manager -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.containers[].command[]?, .items[].spec.containers[].args[]?'; kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-scheduler -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.containers[].command[]?, .items[].spec.containers[].args[]?'; } | grep -- --feature-gates; for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name | cut -d/ -f2); do echo "== $n"; kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/$n/proxy/configz" | jq -c '.kubeletconfig | {featureGates}'; done  # any explicitly enabled alpha gate must have its dependencies enabled too

title: In-place pod resize rejects changes to resources other than cpu and memory

detection.reason: the constraint binds on a future resize request, not on a stored field

quote: Pod resize now only allows CPU and memory resources; other resource types are forbidden.
remediation: Automation that resizes hugepages, ephemeral-storage or extended resources through `pods/resize` gets a validation error after the upgrade; those changes need a pod restart.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resizePolicy != null) | select(.spec.containers[].resources.limits | keys? | map(select(. != "cpu" and . != "memory")) | length != 0) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # resizable pods that also carry a non cpu/memory resource

title: Kubelets now re-authenticate private images per pod — IfNotPresent no longer shares a credentialed image, and imagePullPolicy: Never can fail

detection.reason: whether an image was originally pulled with credentials is kubelet state; pods with `imagePullPolicy: Never` are the ones that can fail outright, so the hint names them

quote: The `KubeletEnsureSecretPulledImages` feature was promoted to Beta and enabled by default.
remediation: A pod that relies on an image another pod pulled with credentials — without presenting its own `imagePullSecrets` — is now re-pulled (IfNotPresent) or fails to start (Never). Give every pod that uses a private image its own pull secret, or set `imagePullCredentialsVerificationPolicy: NeverVerify` in the kubelet config to keep the old behaviour.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].imagePullPolicy == "Never" and (.spec.imagePullSecrets // []) == []) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # these cannot present credentials and fail if their image needed any

title: Service trafficDistribution: PreferClose is deprecated in favour of PreferSameZone
quote: The `PreferClose` value is now deprecated in favor of the more explicit `PreferSameZone`.
remediation: Change `spec.trafficDistribution: PreferClose` to `PreferSameZone` on each Service; the behaviour is identical and the old value keeps working for now.
verifyCommand: kubectl get svc -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.trafficDistribution == "PreferClose") | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # each one should say PreferSameZone

title: DRA partitionable devices (alpha) changed incompatibly — ResourceSlices using counter sets must be removed before the upgrade

detection.reason: ResourceSlices are not collected; pods that reference claims mark the clusters that care

quote: This change introduced backwards-incompatible updates to the alpha feature, requiring any ResourceSlices using it to be removed before upgrading or downgrading between v1.34 and v1.35.
remediation: Only clusters with `DRAPartitionableDevices=true` are affected. Stop the drivers that publish `sharedCounters` / `consumesCounters` slices, delete those ResourceSlices, upgrade, then redeploy a driver release built for 1.35.
verifyCommand: kubectl get resourceslices -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.sharedCounters != null or any(.spec.devices[]?; .consumesCounters != null)) | .metadata.name + " driver=" + .spec.driver'  # these slices must be gone before the control plane upgrade

title: kube-apiserver refuses to start when the request-header CA overlaps the client CA and --requestheader-allowed-names is unset

detection.reason: the CA bundles and the allowed-names flag lives in a component config file or flag on the control plane host, which is not a Kubernetes object the agent collects; the command reads it from the static pod's command line

quote: when `--requestheader-client-ca-file` and `--client-ca-file` contain overlapping certificates, `--requestheader-allowed-names` must be specified so that regular client certificates cannot set authenticating proxy headers for arbitrary users.
remediation: Compare the two CA bundles on each control-plane host; if any certificate appears in both, add `--requestheader-allowed-names=<front-proxy client CN>` (kubeadm sets `front-proxy-client`) before upgrading, or the 1.35 kube-apiserver exits on startup.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-apiserver -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.containers[].command[]?, .items[].spec.containers[].args[]?' | grep -E -- '--(requestheader-client-ca-file|client-ca-file|requestheader-allowed-names)'  # if the two CA files share a certificate, the third flag must be present
